script: Many beginners underprice their work out of fear. Underpricing attracts difficult clients, leaves you exhausted, and makes it hard to raise prices later. So set a price you can defend. Here is a simple method for your first jobs. Step one: estimate the hours the job will take, and add one round of revisions. Step two: multiply those hours by a fair hourly rate. To find a fair rate, check what similar freelancers charge on the same marketplace, and start in the lower middle of that range. Step three: add a small buffer of ten to twenty percent for unexpected work. Step four: compare your price with the value to the client. A sales post that brings in customers is worth more than a plain design. Your first two or three jobs may be discounted to build reviews. Say so clearly, and raise the price for the next client.
